25. The graph shows the observed orbital velocities of stars in a galaxy against their distance from the centre of the galaxy. The core of the galaxy has a radius of 4.0 kpc.
[Graph: velocity / km s$^{-1}$ against radius / kpc with error bars; velocity rises steeply near the centre then remains roughly constant (flat rotation curve)]
(a) Calculate the rotation velocity of stars 4.0 kpc from the centre of the galaxy. The average density of the galaxy is $5.0\times10^{-21}$ kg m$^{-3}$. [2]
(b) Explain why the rotation curves are evidence for the existence of dark matter. [2]
